events.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights Adopted
events.description: The United Nations General Assembly, meeting in Paris, adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights as Resolution 217 A, with 48 votes in favor, none against, and 8 abstentions.
events.significance: It was the first global expression of rights to which all human beings are inherently entitled, and it has since influenced international law, national constitutions, and human rights movements worldwide. Human Rights Day is observed annually on this date.

events.title: First Nobel Prizes Awarded
events.description: The first Nobel Prizes were presented in Stockholm on the fifth anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death, honoring achievements in physics, chemistry, medicine, and literature. Wilhelm Röntgen received the Physics prize for discovering X-rays.
events.significance: The Nobel Prizes became the most prestigious international awards for achievement in science, literature, and peace, and the ceremony continues each year on December 10.

events.title: Theodore Roosevelt Wins the Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: U.S. President Theodore Roosevelt was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for his role in mediating the end of the Russo-Japanese War through the Treaty of Portsmouth.
events.significance: Roosevelt became the first American to win a Nobel Prize in any category, marking the rising role of the United States in international diplomacy.

events.title: Birth of Emily Dickinson
events.description: American poet Emily Dickinson was born in Amherst, Massachusetts. She lived a largely reclusive life and wrote nearly 1,800 poems, very few of which were published during her lifetime.
events.significance: Discovered and published posthumously, her innovative style and themes of death, nature, and immortality made her one of the most important figures in American poetry.

events.title: Wyoming Territory Grants Women the Right to Vote
events.description: The Wyoming Territory passed the first law in the United States granting women the right to vote and hold public office.
events.significance: This milestone for women's suffrage preceded the 19th Amendment by about 50 years and set a precedent for later suffrage victories across the country.
